Authorization settings

Source: R/settings.R
aa_settings.Rd

Builds the settings that control the behavior of the package: password rules, brute-force protection, data retention periods, the list of roles and the interface language. The settings object is passed to the other functions and modules of the package; the package does not use global variables.

Usage

aa_settings(
  max_failed_logins = 5,
  lockout_minutes = 15,
  max_failed_logins_per_minute = 30,
  password_min = 6,
  password_max = 128,
  password_policy = "warn",
  login_max = 64,
  autologin = TRUE,
  session_days = 30,
  session_check_seconds = 30,
  attempts_retention_hours = 24,
  token_retention_days = 30,
  roles = c("admin", "user", "viewer"),
  admin_role = "admin",
  must_change_default = TRUE,
  reset_enabled = FALSE,
  send_reset = NULL,
  reset_base_url = NULL,
  reset_ttl_minutes = 60,
  reset_max_per_hour = 3,
  reset_max_per_minute = 10,
  totp_enabled = FALSE,
  totp_key = NULL,
  totp_issuer = "appauth",
  totp_window = 1,
  google_enabled = FALSE,
  google_client_id = NULL,
  google_client_secret = NULL,
  google_redirect_uri = NULL,
  google_domains = NULL,
  password_login = TRUE,
  registration_enabled = FALSE,
  registration_verify_email = TRUE,
  registration_role = "viewer",
  registration_domains = NULL,
  registration_max_per_hour = 10,
  google_signup = FALSE,
  google_signup_require_domains = TRUE,
  texts = aa_texts("en")
)

Arguments

max_failed_logins

Number of failed sign-in attempts before the login is locked.

lockout_minutes

Window for counting failed attempts and the duration of the lock, in minutes.

max_failed_logins_per_minute

Overall limit of failed sign-in attempts across all logins per minute.

password_min, password_max

Minimum and maximum length of a new password. The limit applies only to new and reset passwords, existing passwords are not affected.

password_policy

What to do with weak new passwords (from the aa_common_passwords() list, equal to the login ignoring case, or made of a single repeated character): "off" do not check, "warn" (default) accept the password but show a warning, "reject" reject the password. Existing passwords are not affected.

login_max

Maximum login length (the login is trimmed and compared exactly, case-sensitively, when attempts are counted).

autologin

Whether to use cookie-based auto sign-in. If FALSE, the user enters the password on every page load and no tokens are issued.

session_days

Lifetime of the auto sign-in token, in days.

session_check_seconds

How often to check that an open session is still allowed (the user has not been blocked or deleted), in seconds.

attempts_retention_hours

How many hours to keep records of sign-in attempts.

token_retention_days

How many days to keep expired and revoked tokens before deleting them.

roles

Allowed user roles.

admin_role

Administrator role, it must be one of roles. Only this role manages users, regardless of the application's permission matrix, and it is the role given to the first created user.

must_change_default

Default state of the "require a password change at next sign-in" checkbox in the add-user dialog and when resetting a password. TRUE (default): a password set by an administrator is temporary, and the administrator clears the checkbox if a change is not needed. FALSE: the checkbox is off, the administrator turns it on.

reset_enabled

Enable password recovery by email: a "Forgot your password?" link appears on the sign-in form. Default FALSE. Requires send_reset and reset_base_url.

send_reset

Function that sends the email, function(email, link, login): sends a message with the link to the email address (for example, using emayili). An error in the function does not interrupt the request and is not visible to the user, the reason goes into the password_reset_requested event.

reset_base_url

Application address the link in the email points to, for example "https://apps.example.com/my_app". It must use https://, except for local development on http://127.0.0.1 or http://localhost. ?reset=<token> is appended to it.

reset_ttl_minutes

Lifetime of the password change link, in minutes.

reset_max_per_hour

How many recovery emails can be sent to one user per hour, further requests are silently ignored.

reset_max_per_minute

Overall limit of recovery emails across all users per minute (protection against spam).

totp_enabled

Enable two-factor authentication (one-time TOTP codes from an authenticator app). Default FALSE. Requires totp_key. Two-factor protection is voluntary: each user enables it in the aa_totp_server() module, and users who have it enabled enter a code when signing in with a password.

totp_key

Encryption key for TOTP secrets in the database, a string of at least 16 characters (for example, from an environment variable). Store it outside the database and outside the repository. If the key is lost or replaced, existing secrets cannot be decrypted and users have to set up 2FA again (an administrator resets it in the user card).

totp_issuer

Service name shown by the authenticator app.

totp_window

How many 30-second steps in each direction of clock drift are tolerated (0 to 5, default 1).

google_enabled

Enable sign-in with Google (OpenID Connect): a "Sign in with Google" button appears on the sign-in form. Default FALSE. Requires google_client_id, google_client_secret and google_redirect_uri. Only a user who already exists in the database and whose email equals the Google account address can sign in. With google_signup = TRUE a new user is created from the verified email; otherwise sign-in never creates users. The role of existing users is taken from the database. The application's two-factor code is not requested for Google sign-in (Google does the verification itself).

google_client_id, google_client_secret

Identifier and secret of the OAuth client (type "Web application") from the Google Cloud Console. Store the secret outside the database and outside the repository (for example, in an environment variable).

google_redirect_uri

Address Google returns the user to: the address of the application as users open it, for example "https://apps.example.com/". It must exactly match an address in the "Authorized redirect URIs" list of the OAuth client. https:// is allowed, and http://localhost for development.

google_domains

Allowed organization domains (a vector, for example c("example.com", "example.net")). If set, sign-in is accepted only for accounts whose signed Google token contains one of these domains (hd, the primary Workspace domain of the organization) and whose email domain is also in the list. If the organization has secondary domains, list both the primary and the secondary ones. An empty value (NULL) disables the domain check, then only the match of the email with a user in the database decides.

password_login

Allow sign-in with a login and password. Default TRUE. FALSE hides the password form and "Forgot your password?" and rejects such attempts on the server; possible only together with google_enabled = TRUE, otherwise there would be no way to sign in. Creating the first administrator on an empty database is still available.

registration_enabled

Allow visitors to create their own accounts from the sign-in form. Default FALSE. The link appears only when the database already has users: on an empty database the first administrator is created as before.

registration_verify_email

Require visitors to confirm their email address before the account is created. Default TRUE. Requires send_reset and reset_base_url; with FALSE the account is created immediately.

registration_role

Role given to self-registered users. Default "viewer". It must be one of roles and cannot be admin_role, so registration never grants administrative rights. Used for both the button and Google sign-up.

registration_domains

Allowed email domains for self-registration (a vector like c("example.com")). NULL (default) allows any domain.

registration_max_per_hour

Maximum number of registration requests per hour across all visitors.

google_signup

Create an account automatically on the first sign-in with Google if the email is not in the database. Default FALSE. Requires google_enabled = TRUE; the login is derived from the email address, the email is taken from the verified Google token, and the role is registration_role.

google_signup_require_domains

Require a non-empty google_domains when google_signup = TRUE. Default TRUE: without a domain check any Google account could create an account. Set to FALSE only for a deliberately open application.

texts

Interface texts, a result of aa_texts().

Value

A list of settings of class aa_settings.

Brute-force protection

If max_failed_logins failed attempts accumulate for one login within lockout_minutes minutes, sign-in for this login is blocked for lockout_minutes minutes starting from the last failed attempt. Attempts made during the lock are not recorded and do not extend the lock. In addition, if max_failed_logins_per_minute failed attempts accumulate over the last minute across all logins together, sign-in is temporarily closed for everyone: this stops password guessing spread over many logins.

Examples

# default settings
settings <- aa_settings()

# password recovery by email
settings <- aa_settings(
  reset_enabled  = TRUE,
  reset_base_url = "https://apps.example.com/my_app",
  send_reset = function(email, link, login) {
    message("Email for ", login, ": ", link)
  }
)

# sign-in with Google (secret from an environment variable), password stays
# as a fallback
settings <- aa_settings(
  google_enabled       = TRUE,
  google_client_id     = "1234-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com",
  google_client_secret = Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET", "secret"),
  google_redirect_uri  = "https://apps.example.com/",
  google_domains       = c("example.com", "example.net")
)

# open registration with email confirmation and Google sign-up
settings <- aa_settings(
  registration_enabled = TRUE,
  google_enabled       = TRUE,
  google_signup        = TRUE,
  google_client_id     = "1234-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com",
  google_client_secret = Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET", "secret"),
  google_redirect_uri  = "https://apps.example.com/",
  google_domains       = c("example.com"),
  reset_base_url       = "https://apps.example.com/my_app",
  send_reset = function(email, link, login) {
    message("Email for ", login, ": ", link)
  }
)

# stricter protection, Russian interface and custom roles
settings <- aa_settings(
  max_failed_logins = 3,
  lockout_minutes   = 30,
  password_min      = 10,
  roles             = c("admin", "editor", "viewer"),
  texts             = aa_texts("ru")
)
settings$lockout_minutes
#> [1] 30
